new_statements.relation_note: pitch accent attributed to Northern and Citak Asmat; Kamoro said to have an Una-like system per Donohue's fieldnotes
new_statements.rule_in_words: North Asmat is classed (tentatively, 'seem to') as a pitch accent language, grouped with Citak Asmat, on the authority of Donohue 1997; nothing on the position of the accent or on stress.
new_statements.identity_note: 'North Asmat' / 'Northern.. Asmat varieties' in a TNG-wide tone survey that otherwise follows Voorhoeve's Asmat divisions (Central, Casuarina Coast, Citak, North); almost certainly = Voorhoeve's North Asmat = nort2917, though Roesler's two-tone analysis of the Ayam variety (north-western Central Asmat, Voorhoeve 1980:22) is a conceivable source of confusion. Secondhand: cites Donohue 1997, whose own basis for North Asmat is unknown (Voorhoeve 1980, the only NA data, says NA was never phonemicised). | Group-level generalisation over 'the Asmat-Kamoro group' (which in this chapter's inventory includes Momogo-Pupis-Irogo [nks]); North Asmat is not named in the prosody passage. Secondhand (summarises Donohue 1997). Listed because our bibliography files this chapter as 'read: silent on stress' while it does carry a tone statement bearing on the group, and because it reads Donohue 1997 differently from Ross 2005 (work 1 of A). | Family-survey notes on 'Asmat' as one language; the author states 'The following notes are based on the writer's own description of the language', i.e. the Flamingo Bay sub-dialect of the Central-Coast (Kawenak) dialect = Central Asmat (cent2117). The Momogo-Pupis-Irogo villages are not mentioned; Drabbe's 'Northern dialect on the upper Lorentz and Noord Rivers' in the same paragraph is Keenok (also Central Asmat per Voorhoeve 1980). Useful only as the general Asmat statement that Ross/Donohue-type classifications depart from.

new_statements.quote: The various TNG subgroups in this region largely lack pitch accent prosody. This holds for most Awyu-Dumut languages, the Kayagar group and the Asmat-Kamoro group. However, northern members of Awyu-Dumut, who are in close contact with people of the central highlands, do have pitch accent. Similarly, most members of the Asmat-Kamoro group lack tonal prosody but Kamoro and Citak Asmat are tonal and these are in contact with cordilleran languages.

new_statements.relation_note: no tone / pitch accent in most Asmat-Kamoro languages; Kamoro and Citak Asmat tonal; no stress statement for any Asmat variety
new_statements.rule_in_words: Most Asmat-Kamoro languages are said to lack tone/pitch accent prosody, the exceptions being Kamoro and Citak Asmat; by implication the non-Citak Asmat languages (which would include North Asmat) are non-tonal. Nothing on stress placement.
new_statements.exceptions: Kamoro and Citak Asmat are tonal (contact with cordilleran languages)
